channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japan's Yen sleeps through a regional equity crash
item.description: The Yen trades a fraction under 164.00 on Tuesday, marginally weaker on the day, inside a 30-pip band with a floor above 163.50 and a high a few ticks beneath the standing cycle extreme.

item.title: The Australian Dollar sells a speech and waits for the number that decides August
item.description: The Aussie trades just beneath 0.7000 on Tuesday, down around 0.25% and last in the G10 queue, after a Sydney address from the Reserve Bank of Australia's Governor gave the hike case nothing to eat.

item.title: The Euro finally gets cheaper energy, and that is the problem
item.description: The Euro trades just under 1.1400 on Tuesday, around 0.15% firmer, after a session that ran from a shade above 1.1350 to a fraction over 1.1400.

item.title: British Pound Sterling waits on a forecast the tape has already outrun
item.description: The Pound spends Tuesday almost perfectly still, trading just under 1.3300 with a session range under 40 pips between a floor above 1.3250 and a ceiling fractionally above 1.3300.

item.title: Indonesia: Policy focus after BI Governor exit – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao analyzes Indonesia markets after Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo’s unexpected resignation. She notes initial weakness in onshore assets as investors reassess implications for Rupiah stability and bonds.

item.title: Australia CPI could boost Aussie if inflation arrives above 4%
item.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) will publish the June Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Wednesday at 01:30 GMT. The report is expected to show that inflation rose 4% from a year earlier, matching the May reading. The monthly CPI is foreseen at 0.2% following the -0.7% print from May.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS tightening keeps pair under pressure – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy for a second straight meeting, slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope while leaving the band’s centre and width unchanged.

item.title: NZD/USD holds ahead of the Fed's decision
item.description: NZD/USD trades nearly unchanged around the 0.5785 area on Tuesday, struggling to extend its earlier recovery despite a modest decline in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Brazilian Real: BRL seen weaker into year-end – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s strategists Mauricio Une and Renan Alves note that tensions between the United States (US) and Iran have eased slightly with a pause in hostilities, but the outlook for global energy and markets remains highly uncertain.

item.title: United States: Supercore and measurement debates shape Fed path – BNY
item.description: BNY strategists John Velis and David Tam see elevated US supercore inflation as a key argument for further tightening but still favor a July hold.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar eases ahead of Fed as Oil and Gold extend losses
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades slightly lower on Tuesday as investors reduce some exposure ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Mexican Peso advances within range against the US Dollar
item.description: USD/MXN trades around 17.40 on Tuesday, posting modest losses for a third consecutive session. The US Dollar (USD) retains a broadly firm tone despite softer-than-expected United States (US) data, as investors await the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement on Wednesday.

item.title: Silver: Forecast cut but deficit supports upside – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke reports that Silver has fallen from USD 70 to USD 57.50 per troy ounce and that the bank has lowered its forecasts, now seeing USD 67 by year-end and USD 80 by end‑2027.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds as markets await Tokyo inflation data
item.description: USD/JPY trades slightly higher near the 163.80 area on Tuesday, remaining close to multi-decade highs as the Japanese Yen (JPY) struggles to attract demand. Softer United States (US) consumer confidence data limited the US Dollar’s advance, although the pair maintained its upward bias.

item.title: Swiss Franc steadies against US Dollar as Fed decision looms
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) steadies against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as the Greenback gives up its early gains, with traders turning cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement on Wednesday.

item.title: The chip rout is funding the Dow Jones Industrial Average's record chase
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades just short of 52,900 on Tuesday, higher by close to 700 points and 1.3%, roughly 450 points beneath the record it set in the first week of July. Taken alone, that reads as a broad risk rally.

item.title: The Euro is not rallying, the British Pound Sterling is being demoted
item.description: The Euro is on track for its eighth gain in nine sessions against the Pound, and the explanation that would normally cover a run of that length is not available.

item.title: Silver loses ground as hopes for US-Iran deal improve risk appetite
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $57.40 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 1.7% on the day. The white metal is under pressure as the US Dollar (USD) loses some strength and investors reduce their exposure to safe-haven assets ahead of the Federal Reserve's (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bears target the 200-day SMA after losing the $80 mark
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil extends its decline on Tuesday after falling 9% the previous day following a pause in attacks between the United States and Iran. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $77.90, down nearly 4% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar Index eases from tops, back to 101.30 ahead of Fed
item.description: The Greenback, when tracked by the US Dollar Index (DXY), abandons the area of monthly peaks and recedes toward the 101.30 zone on turnaround Tuesday.

item.title: Euro skyrockets amid softer US confidence
item.description: EUR/USD trades higher near the 1.1400 area on Tuesday, gaining around 0.3% as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following softer United States (US) consumer-confidence data. The US Dollar Index falls toward 101.30, helping the Euro extend its recovery.

item.title: Gold: Hawkish Fed delays Gold recovery path – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch and Thu Lan Nguyen note that the Gold price has dropped nearly 30% from its January record as higher real yields and hawkish Federal Reserve expectations weigh on the metal.

item.title: Oil: Weakens on deal hopes and fragile flows – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Brent has sold off sharply as US–Iran strikes pause and President Trump signals a “good chance” of a deal. They stress that flows through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, as well as Black Sea exports, remain critical.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds onto losses after Bullock keeps further rate hikes on the table
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near the 0.6970 area on Tuesday, falling around 0.3% as the Australian Dollar (AUD) comes under pressure despite hawkish remarks from Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock.

item.title: British Pound Sterling has nothing to say in front of two central banks
item.description: The Pound trades near 1.3300 in the New York morning, effectively flat on a session that has run barely 30 pips between a floor a shade above 1.3250 and a ceiling fractionally above the 1.3300 handle.

item.title: British Pound: Bearish reversal extends before BoE – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report GBP/USD is extending its bearish reversal toward early-July levels as markets scale back Bank of England (BoE) tightening expectations. September pricing has been cut and cumulative hikes by December reduced.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD sits out the panic it was built for
item.description: Gold trades near $4,020 in the Tuesday New York morning, down roughly 1.4% on a session that started near $4,075 and never built a bid.

item.title: $4,000: Gold’s key support faces a crucial Fed test
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Tuesday, pressured by a firmer US Dollar (USD), even as Oil prices extend their pullback on hopes of an end to the US-Iran war.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA keeps hike option alive – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock signaled a possible rate hike at the August 10–11 meeting, stressing inflation is still too high and productivity weak.

item.title: Canadian Dollar benefits from softer US Dollar despite lower Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD trades near 1.4105 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 0.14% on the day, though the pair remains close to its recent highs as traders refrain from taking aggressive positions ahead of the Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy decision.
